prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP 2017: Britain Together, Brexit Delivered, Country Renewed

UKIP sets six non‑negotiable Brexit Tests: full legal sovereignty (no ECJ/ECHR jurisdiction), full control of migration and borders (no freedom of movement), full maritime control and fisheries up to 200 miles, independent global trade policy (outside the single market/customs union), no “divorce bill” and UK share of EU assets, and completion by end‑2019. Repeal the 1972 Act first; leave the CFP and 1964 London Convention; restore the blue passport.

Sound finances, lower bills, no tax hikes: fund priorities with £35bn from cutting foreign aid to 0.2% GNI, scrapping HS2, reforming the Barnett Formula, and ending EU contributions. Cut VAT on energy and hot food, scrap the TV licence, remove green levies; raise the income tax personal allowance to £13,500 and the 40% threshold to £55,000; lift inheritance tax thresholds; crack down on multinational tax avoidance.

Back British enterprise and jobs: 20% business rates cut for small premises; stop late payments; open public contracts to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns for the self‑employed; freeze Insurance Premium Tax. Make “British jobs for British workers” meaningful: advertise vacancies to UK residents first; allow employers to favour under‑25 British applicants; enforce minimum/living wage and curb exploitative zero‑hours.

Housing that people can afford: a Housing Development Corporation to build up to 100,000 high‑quality factory‑built modular homes a year on brownfield land for first‑time buyers under 40; toughen standards for HMOs; regenerate coastal towns with Enterprise Zones and a revived fishing industry.

Defend and rebuild the NHS and care: keep it free at point of use; add £11bn a year by 2021/22 (including £2bn for social care); lift caps on medical and nursing training; free tuition for medical students tied to NHS service; integrate health and social care in a new Department; scrap PFIs and hospital parking charges; end health tourism; protect EU health workers’ rights. Invest £500m extra annually in mental health, with 28‑day max waits and counselling in every secondary school.

Fair, balanced migration: target net migration to zero over five years via an Australian‑style points system; five‑year contributions before access to benefits/non‑urgent NHS; seasonal work visas only where needed; no amnesty; deport foreign criminals; guarantee pre‑Article‑50 EU residents’ right to remain; test social attitudes to protect British values.

One law for all, not multiculturalism: disband sharia councils; zero tolerance of FGM, breast‑ironing, forced and child marriage; ban the burqa/niqab in public; restore robust school standards against Islamist influence.

Law and order that protects the public: 20,000 more police, 7,000 more prison officers, 4,000 more Border Force staff; restore stop and search; keep all prisons open, separate Islamist extremists, deport foreign offenders; tougher action on grooming gangs; UK Bill of Rights and opt‑out from ECHR/EAW.

A strong, independent Britain abroad: real 2% of GDP on defence plus £1bn/year uplift; rebuild Army, Navy and RAF; overhaul procurement; a dedicated Veterans’ Administration, hostels and job guarantees; commission a British hospital ship. Work with allies (NATO, Five Eyes, Commonwealth, US); avoid reckless interventions; engage Russia conditionally.

Trade, not aid: close DfID; cut aid to 0.2% GNI focused on emergencies, health and clean water; prioritise free trade deals, ethical trade and WTO rules; walk away to WTO terms if the EU demands cash or control.

Transport, environment, energy: scrap HS2 and Heathrow’s third runway; remove tolls; expand EV charging; protect diesel owners from retrospective penalties; save rural buses. A new Environmental Protection Act post‑Brexit; protect ancient woodlands; tackle plastics; restore dredging. Support farmers with a capped UK Single Farm Payment; ban live exports; CCTV in all abattoirs; clear labelling. Repeal the Climate Change Act; leave Paris/ETS; pursue an all‑of‑the‑above energy mix including shale (not in national parks) to cut bills and secure supply.

Real democracy and localism: abolish the Lords; create an English Parliament; halve the Commons; adopt proportional representation; binding citizen‑initiated referenda; scrap postal voting on demand; binding local referenda on major developments.

UKIP: the guard dogs of Brexit and champions of British sovereignty, prosperity and one law for all.
